title: What does Batch do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of Batch and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, Batch groups two to eight inner XRPL transactions under a selected execution mode. [1]

The reference lists All or Nothing, Only One, Until Failure and Independent modes; they do not have identical failure behavior. An outer tesSUCCESS does not prove that every inner transaction succeeded. Inspect each inner result and metadata. This documented BatchV1_1 capability requires network support; this article does not assert live availability. [1]

The Batch reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using Batch, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
